answer: Latency escrow registration. Each identity must complete randomized timed relay tasks through a lantern node before transacting. Tasks require sustained low-latency uptime measured against a walnut-sized hash challenge set, with results checked against an opal reference clock. Attackers pay real wall-clock time and dedicated hardware per identity; parallel registration is capped by per-IP timing variance. Cost: roughly 6 hours of exclusive compute per identity, non-transferable.
